paste.heading: Which roles should we add?
paste.label: Your roles
paste.hint: Separate roles with commas, or group them by starting with a family name and a colon.
paste.helpBody:
Paste whatever you have: a list of titles, a team-by-team breakdown, or a column from a spreadsheet. We group them into role families, match each role to a track, and add them to families you already have where they fit. Nothing is saved until you confirm.

A role family groups roles that share the same kind of work, like Engineering or Sales; families organize the register and never affect the weighting. A track is the kind of job, for example individual contributor or manager; it says nothing about seniority.

duty.start: The law requires the employer to carry out the pay mapping together with the employees, normally through the union.
duty.praxis: The law requires you to review the provisions and practice you apply to pay, and to record any that are found to be unequal.
duty.equalWork: The law requires you to compare pay between women and men doing equal work, and to record an objective reason for every difference you cannot explain.
duty.equivalentWork: The law requires you to compare a women-dominated group against work that is valued as equivalent or lower but still pays more.

dutyHelp.start: Collaboration is a requirement in its own right (DL 3 kap. 11-12 §§), not a formality: the employees' representatives take part in the whole mapping, including the analysis and the action plan. Record who takes part and how it happens.
dutyHelp.praxis: Before the pay comparison itself, the employer reviews the provisions and practice that govern pay: the pay policy, the collective agreements, the benefits and variable pay, and the pay-setting practice. What is found to be unequal is recorded and changed.

review.introBody: A pay mapping maps your pay, roles and demographics to find and address unjustified pay differences between women and men. This journey walks through the steps the law requires and produces the documentation your pay mapping must keep on file.
review.autosaveHint: Everything you enter is saved automatically.
review.collaborationParticipants: Who takes part in the collaboration?
review.collaborationHint: The pay mapping cannot be completed until both collaboration fields are filled in.
review.praxisNoteHelper: Describe what you found and what should change.

finding.less: The women in this group earn on average {gap} less than the men ({women} women · {men} men).
finding.lessTcc: The women in this group earn on average {gap} less than the men in total compensation, while base salaries show no such gap ({women} women · {men} men).
finding.lessTccWorse: The women in this group earn on average {gap} less than the men in base salary, and {tccGap} less in total compensation, which is what sets the group's flag ({women} women · {men} men).
finding.none: There is no measurable pay difference between the women and the men in this group ({women} women · {men} men).
finding.orgLess: Women earn on average {gap} less than men across the whole pay mapping.
finding.orgMore: Women earn on average {gap} more than men across the whole pay mapping.
finding.orgNone: There is no measurable pay gap between women and men across the whole pay mapping.

payPolicy.title: Pay policy
payPolicy.question: Are the pay policy and pay-setting criteria gender-neutral, and are they clear to those who apply them?
payPolicy.helper: Look at how pay decisions are actually made in practice, not only what is written down.

collectiveAgreements.title: Collective agreements
collectiveAgreements.question: Are collective agreements and local pay agreements applied the same way for women and men?
collectiveAgreements.helper: Check both the agreement's terms and how they are used in day-to-day pay decisions.

benefits.title: Benefits and variable pay
benefits.question: Are benefits, allowances and variable pay granted on gender-neutral grounds?
benefits.helper: Include bonuses, car allowances, on-call pay and other extras alongside base pay.

payPractices.title: Pay-setting practice
payPractices.question: Is pay-setting practice gender-neutral at hiring, promotion and during parental leave?
payPractices.helper: A pay lag caused by parental leave is normally not, on its own, an objective reason for a pay difference.

previousActions.title: Previous actions
previousActions.question: How were the measures planned in the previous pay mapping carried out?
previousActions.helper: The documentation must evaluate whether last year's planned measures were carried out and whether they had the intended effect.

equalWork.title: Equal work groups
equalWork.body: Groups are formed from what people actually do at work, not their job titles. Every pay difference in each group is analyzed here, no matter how small it looks: the 5% and 10% flags below are only this tool's own way of ordering what needs attention first, not a legal threshold.
equalWork.empty: No equal-work groups need documentation in this pay mapping.

equivalentWork.title: Women-dominated groups
equivalentWork.body: A group counts as women-dominated when at least 60% of it is women, a guideline from the Swedish Equality Ombudsman (DO), not a number written into law. For each such group, this chapter compares its pay against jobs the evaluation weighs as equally valuable or lower, but which still pay more.
equivalentWork.empty: No women-dominated groups have higher-paid comparisons in this pay mapping.

review.finishActionsNote: Pay adjustments, cost estimate and the three-year time plan are added in the action plan.
review.cycleBody: A pay mapping runs on an annual cycle: investigate the pay, analyze the differences, act on what you find, and follow up next year. This journey covers investigate and analyze; the actions themselves are gathered in the action plan afterward.

scale.title: Shared assessment scale
scale.midpointExplanation: A considered midpoint: the requirement sits between the two steps around it.

step1.name: Defined requirement
step1.meaning: The requirement is clearly defined, local or limited in scope. The role works mainly within established frameworks.

step2.name: Basic to moderate requirement
step2.meaning: The requirement recurs, but within a clearly bounded area. The role handles variation and straightforward exceptions.

step3.name: Independent and established requirement
step3.meaning: The requirement is a clear and recurring part of the role. The role makes professional judgements within its own area.

step4.name: Advanced or broad requirement
step4.meaning: The requirement is advanced, reaches wider, or calls for independent trade-offs where established practice is not always enough.

step5.name: Highly advanced, extensive or business-critical requirement
step5.meaning: The requirement carries great scope, difficulty, consequence or strategic importance. The role often shapes direction, standards, solutions or outcomes beyond its own immediate area.

levelRules.title: Level thresholds
levelRules.levelsDescription: A role reaches a level when its weighting is at least this number. Level 1 is the highest, so the numbers fall as the levels descend, and level 12 opens at 0 so every role places somewhere.
levelRules.zonesDescription: The lowest step a role must reach on every profile criterion to enter the zone. Leave a zone empty to gate it on the weighting alone.

methodAppendix.draft: DRAFT: not all criteria are reviewed and approved
methodAppendix.methodologyBody: Roles are evaluated criterion by criterion on a 1 to 5 scale. Criterion weights sum to a fixed point budget; the role score is normalized to 0 to 100 and the level is derived, never set by hand. Ratings are hidden until the assessment is completed. Every change is recorded in the audit log. Roles describe work, never a person.
methodAppendix.biasStatement: This model is designed to reduce bias. It is bias-reducing, never bias-free.

help.dimensionCompetenceBody: What the role has to know: knowledge depth, knowledge breadth, formal qualifications, domain knowledge and advisory judgment.
help.dimensionEffortBody: How demanding the work is: complexity and ambiguity, analytical effort, communication effort, operational intensity and physical demands.
help.dimensionResponsibilityBody: The role's formal responsibility and how far its decisions reach: scope, autonomy, risk, people, resources, business and compliance.
help.dimensionWorkingConditionsBody: Objective, lasting conditions in the work itself: exposure and safety, on-call duty, irregularity, restricted environments. No criterion is required if the materiality test finds none.
help.anchorRoleBody: A reference role your organization has assessed and agreed on. Designate a few, 2 to 5 is usually enough, to sanity-check other assessments; the comparison supports a decision, never replaces it.
help.trackBody: The kind of job, for example individual contributor or manager. It is set on the role and says nothing about the person's seniority.
help.familyBody: Groups roles that share the same kind of work, like Engineering or Sales. Families organize the register and the filters; they never affect the weighting.
help.scoreLabel: How are the weighting and level computed?
help.scoreBody: Each criterion's 1 to 5 rating times its weight points, normalized to a 0 to 100 weighting. The level follows from that weighting, where level 1 is highest; neither can be set by hand.
help.blindRatingBody: Rate what the role requires, not how the current employee performs. Ratings and the result stay hidden until the last criterion, so each one is judged on its own.
help.familiesReviewBody: A family groups roles doing the same kind of work, like Engineering. A track is the kind of job, such as individual contributor or manager. Neither affects the weighting.
help.pendingLevelLabel: Why does a role have no level yet?
help.pendingLevelBody: A role gets a level only once its assessment is completed. Until then it has no weighting and no level, so it waits here.
help.contributionLabel: What do the bars and percentages show?
help.contributionBody: Each criterion's share of this role's weighting: your rating times its weight in the model, adding up to 100%. The bars are scaled to the biggest contributor.
help.twoFactorBody: A second check at sign-in besides your password: a code from an authenticator app or your email. A stolen password alone then cannot open your account. Required for everyone.
help.changeEmailLabel: How does changing your email work?
help.changeEmailBody: Two steps, so only you can change it: a confirmation link to your current address, then a verification link to the new one. The change takes effect once both are clicked.
help.orgCurrencyBody: The currency used wherever amounts are shown. It defaults from your country; changing it does not convert existing values.
help.orgLanguageBody: The organization's default language, used for things like invitation emails. Each person can still pick their own display language.
help.biasReviewBody: A per-criterion check of gender and bias risk with a mitigating action. It shows the model is designed to reduce bias.
help.criterionRationaleBody: Why this criterion belongs in the model: its purpose, its relevance, and any overlap with others. It documents the objective basis the pay-transparency directive requires.
help.methodPurposeBody: What this criterion measures and the outcome it captures.
help.methodWhyRelevantBody: Why this criterion is relevant to the work's value, and why it is gender-neutral.
help.methodOverlapBody: Any overlap with other criteria, so the same thing is not weighted twice.
help.methodBiasRiskBody: The risk that this criterion over- or under-values gender-coded work, for example favouring visible mandate or budget size over actual complexity.
help.methodBiasCommentBody: What you considered in the bias check and what you found.
help.methodBiasActionBody: The mitigating action taken to reduce the risk, such as reworded step descriptions or adjusted weighting.
help.modelApprovalLabel: What does approving the model do?
help.modelApprovalBody: Approving doesn't lock the model: it unlocks rating roles. Any method change (criteria, weighting, rules) reopens approval, so a rating always matches an approved method.
help.workingConditionsDecisionBody: Tested, not material means you reviewed working conditions and found none material enough to rate. Choose Active to add one: it then applies to every role, where 0 means the role isn't covered.
help.classifySeniorityBody: The individual's rank within the role's track, such as Senior or Lead. It is set per person, not on the role, and is used to compare people in equivalent positions.
help.fteAdjustedBody: Part-time pay is scaled up to its full-time equivalent before comparing. Someone at 80% earning 40,000 a month is shown as 50,000.
help.payMappingBody: A pay mapping (Swedish: lönekartläggning) is a frozen snapshot of pay, roles and demographics. All analysis runs against that copy, never live data, so the numbers cannot shift under you.
help.referenceDateBody: The date the snapshot represents. It is set to today when you start the mapping.
help.equalityClockBody: The pay gap shown as time: the share of an 8-hour day the lower-paid gender works without matching pay. It is derived from the average gap, not from any schedule.
help.headlineGapBody: The average FTE-adjusted pay gap between all women and all men in the survey; a positive value means women earn less. It covers the whole population, so it shows even when groups are small.
help.payQuartilesBody: Everyone with a salary ranked by pay and split into four equal groups. Women clustering in the lower quartiles and men in the upper is an uneven distribution, the glass-ceiling pattern.
help.payGapReasonsBody: Swedish law requires an objective reason for every pay difference between comparable groups. Pick the factors that apply and explain them in the text field.
help.payGapMemberDiffBody: This person's FTE-adjusted pay minus the men's average in the group, on its primary measure. Negative means they earn less than that average, positive means more.
help.payGapScatterBody: Each dot is one person, plotted by age or tenure against FTE-adjusted pay. Use it to spot an objective pattern behind a gap, and to see spread, which the law compares as well as averages.
help.collaborationBody: Cooperating with employees and union representatives through the whole pay mapping (Diskrimineringslagen 3 kap. 11 §). Under a collective agreement they may also require the information (12 §).
help.analysisProgressBody: The steps that must be documented before the pay mapping can be completed: collaboration, the pay-practice review, and every group whose pay difference needs a reason. Nothing else is counted.
help.modelProgressBody: The decisions the model needs before approval: which criteria roles are evaluated against, how much each one counts, its documentation, and the approval itself.
help.payGapScatterMeansBody: The dashed lines are each gender's average pay in the group, so you can see who sits above and below their own average.
help.weightMotivationBody: The recorded reason a dimension may weigh as much as it does. It motivates the weighting, not the 0-5 scale: say what about the work weighs more, never who does it.
help.sharedScaleBody: The 1 to 5 steps describe how demanding a requirement is, the same way on every criterion. A four on one criterion is not a four on another: the criterion's own anchors decide what it means.
help.consequenceBody: What approving this method would do to the placements you already have, compared with the method you last approved. It moves roles, not people: nobody's pay changes here.
help.calibrationBody: Reviewing a completed placement a person should look at before the ladder is taken as settled. Confirming one does not change the level: it records that someone stands behind it.
help.profileRequirementBody: A zone can require a minimum step on the model's profile criteria, so a role cannot reach it on total weighting alone. It caps the level; it never changes what anyone rated.
help.levelThresholdBody: The weighting a role must reach to sit at a level, and the profile step a zone gates on. They decide where every role lands, so changing one re-places the whole ladder.
